correctness.rationale: The Gram matrix has diagonal 4 and conjugate off-diagonal entries of magnitude |z_S|<4, so determinant, smallest eigenvalue, inverse trace and squared sampler condition number have strict monotonic dependence on |z_S| in the required direction. For four unit roots summing to zero, both odd coefficients of the monic polynomial vanish by conjugacy; evenness forces two antipodal pairs. On an odd grid, the two opposite-side pairings of a cyclically ordered quadrilateral cannot both have equal opposite chord lengths (that would yield an inscribed parallelogram and hence antipodes). For an unequal pairing, the reverse triangle inequality and the strictly increasing consecutive drops in 2 cos(pi d/N) give the first drop as lower bound. Equality forces distances 1,2 and opposite pair-sum phases, which gives exactly b=a+(N-1)/2 for the distance-two pair's start. This construction is distinct-site even for N=5; an odd cyclic group has no nontrivial translation stabilizer of a four-set. The stated asymptotics and covariance ratio follow by expansion and the fixed trace. Separate 45-digit computations of squared magnitudes using the six pairwise cosine contributions on 230300 anchored four-sets for N=4..50 recover the optimizer families after translations.
residual_risks: Numerical enumeration is corroboration only, and does not certify exact ties or the all-orders proof. The variance interpretation assumes the stated observation covariance and the normalization in the record.
